blocking_findings.description: The claimed every-active-boundary control deduplicates observations into subject/path sets. It cannot distinguish two declarations checking the same field under different contracts, or detect omission of a repeated obligation. An isolated mutation caching record.field results only by subject/path survived all 261 replayed direct controls and 143 SQLite-path controls. With two declarations for note, one accepting text and the second requiring a different literal, that mutant returned AVAILABLE with no diagnostics; the unchanged implementation correctly rejected the second contract. Thus the current tests do not prove the sealed per-declaration consumption guarantee.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Track independently expected boundary obligations with enough identity to distinguish declarations and contracts, preserving necessary multiplicity. Add direct and retained controls where repeated access to the same exact field has distinct contracts, and require bypassing the second check to fail the intended diagnostic/support assertion.

blocking_findings.description: The new dependency-unavailable rejection site lacks its required exact diagnostic assertion and deletion-sensitive control. The Probes ledger explicitly lists this as G02c, but no test asserts the reason 'dependency unavailable' and the mutation list does not remove this guard. Replacing its diagnostic append with pass survived all 261 replayed direct controls and 143 SQLite-path controls because existing rejection assertions are satisfied by other diagnostics.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Add a focused control asserting the literal prerequisite subject, path, UNKNOWN state and dependency-unavailable reason, with a valid counterpart. Include an isolated deletion experiment that fails specifically because this diagnostic disappears, and reconcile the guard ledger with the implemented controls.
